review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the sibling DG files (Twisted/Basic.lean, ShiftClosure/CochainComplex.lean, Functor/Basic.lean) to check how simp lemmas are used there. I did not find any loop or competing-rule problem. The `simp↓` lemmas `dgHomEquiv_dgDifferential`, `dgHomEquiv_dgComp` and `dgHomEquiv_dgId` rewrite a `dgHomEquiv` of a shift-closure operation into `C`-level operations. Their right-hand sides are `C`-level terms, so they should not re-trigger the left-hand sides. One gap is that `dgMap_ι` is not a simp lemma. `ι_obj` and `dgHomEquiv_ιHomEquiv` are simp, but `dgMap_ι` is the only lemma that links `(ι R).dgMap` to `ιHomEquiv`. The sibling lemma `dgMap_embedding` is `@[simp]`. The adjacent non-simp lemmas `dgHomComplex_eq` (a definitional unfolding) and `dgHomEquiv_negOnePow_smul_dgComp` (the Keller-order variant) are reasonably left non-simp. I have not run Lean, so the downstream effect of this change is untested.

findings.excerpt: theorem dgMap_ι {X Y : C} {n : ℤ} (f : DGHom R n X Y) : (ι R).dgMap n f = ιHomEquiv R X Y n f :=
findings.problem: `dgMap_ι` is the only lemma that turns `(ι R).dgMap n f` into `ιHomEquiv R X Y n f`, and it has no `@[simp]` attribute. The file does mark `ι_obj` and `dgHomEquiv_ιHomEquiv` as `@[simp]`. `dgHomEquiv_ιHomEquiv` has `ιHomEquiv` on its left-hand side, so it can only fire once `dgMap_ι` has produced an `ιHomEquiv` term. Without `dgMap_ι` in the simp set, the simp chain `dgMap` → `ιHomEquiv` → `dgHomEquiv`/`XIsoOfEq` stops at the first step, and `simp` does not simplify `dgHomEquiv R ⟨X,0⟩ ⟨Y,0⟩ n ((ι R).dgMap n f)`. The analogous lemma `dgMap_embedding` for the twisted-object embedding is `@[simp]`, so this file is inconsistent with its sibling. A later file (`CochainComplex.lean`) has `dgMap_toCochainComplex`, which is also not simp.
findings.proposed_change:
Mark the lemma `@[simp]`, as `dgMap_embedding` is:
```
/-- The inclusion acts on morphisms by `TauCeti.DGShiftClosure.ιHomEquiv`. -/
@[simp]
theorem dgMap_ι ...
```
I see no cycle risk: the right-hand side `ιHomEquiv R X Y n f` is rewritten onward only by `dgHomEquiv_ιHomEquiv`, and only when it sits under `dgHomEquiv`. The generic `EnrichedFunctor.dgMap_dgDifferential`, `dgMap_dgComp` and `dgMap_dgId` lemmas push `dgMap` inward first, and `dgMap_ι` then fires on the atoms.
findings.benefit: Goals about `(ι R).dgMap n f` would normalize through the existing simp lemmas `dgHomEquiv_ιHomEquiv` and `ι_obj`. Users would no longer need to `rw [dgMap_ι]` by hand before those lemmas apply. The simp interface of `ι` would then match that of `DGTwistedObject.embedding`.
